STUDYQURAN:41:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:intro/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:41:intro/r8.claim: Believers and disbelievers are juxtaposed in 29–32, followed by exhortation to respectful conduct even with disbelievers (33–39), then discussion of the Quran and its rejecters (40–46).
STUDYQURAN:41:intro/r8.anchor: an exhortation to the believers to maintain respectful speech and conduct even with the disbelievers (vv. 33–39)

THALABI:v8p297/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p297/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p297/r7.claim: A barren, dry earth revived by rain proves that the One who revives it can also revive the dead.
THALABI:v8p297/r7.anchor: إن الذي أحياها لمحي الموتى إنه على كل شيء قدير

ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r16.claim: The dry earth is portrayed as a humbled person with a bowed neck; the comparison warns the arrogant and signals that the humble will rise.
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r16.anchor: Arz’ın hüsran ve kuraklık hâlindeki perişanlığı zillete düşmüş bir kimsenin boynunu büktüğü huşû‘, yani tezellül hâline benzetilmiştir

ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r17.claim: Rain makes the earth stir and swell; the One who revives it can revive the dead and has power over everything, so believers should persist in calling to God.
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r17.anchor: elbette ölüleri dirilticidir. Rûhsuz cesedlere rûh verir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p62/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p62/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p62/r6.claim: Arguments from the surrounding world reinforce God's oneness and the Hereafter, and opposition to these clear signs is condemned.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p62/r6.anchor: The argument stated in the beginning of the sūrah in favour of tawḥīd and the Hereafter is reinforced by certain other arguments found in the world around man.

ASAD-NOTES:41:38#n34/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:41:38#n34/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:41:38#n34/r1.claim: Although earth's revival often symbolizes bodily resurrection, here it illustrates God's power to give spiritual life to hearts closed to His existence and omnipotence.
ASAD-NOTES:41:38#n34/r1.anchor: it appears to be an illustration of God's power to bestow spiritual life upon hearts

ASAD-NOTES:41:38#n34/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:41:38#n34/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:41:38#n34/r2.claim: The verse calls believers not to abandon hope that those denying truth may one day understand the Qur'anic message.
ASAD-NOTES:41:38#n34/r2.anchor: call to the believer never to abandon the hope that "those who deny the truth" may one day grasp the truth

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p121/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p121/r1.speaker: عبد القاهر
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p121/r1.claim: Abd al-Qahir directs grammatical meanings to their places in the discourse's order, rather than treating parsing as a craft detached from meaning.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p121/r1.anchor: عند عبد القاهر، أن يفهم هذا الإعجاز البلاغي في النظم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p121/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p121/r2.speaker: عبد القاهر
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p121/r2.claim: His Dalail al-Ijaz presents the knowledge of eloquence as a means to understand the Qur'an's inimitability; a word's excellence depends on how its meaning fits neighboring meanings.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p121/r2.anchor: وكتابه (دلائل الإعجاز) يُفَصَّل القول في هذا العلم الشريف بما يتفاضل به الكلام في نظمه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p121/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p121/r3.speaker: عبد القاهر
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p121/r3.claim: Words do not differ in merit as isolated forms: fit with adjacent words gives them virtue, and the same word can please in one position yet feel heavy in another.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p121/r3.anchor: فالألفاظ لا تتفاضل من حيث هي ألفاظ مجردة، ولا من حيث هي كلم مفردة

QIRAAT-ER:41:39:15#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:41:39:15#1/r1.speaker: H
QIRAAT-ER:41:39:15#1/r1.claim: The ten-reading variant adds hamza after bāʾ, shifting the sound and potentially foregrounding elevation rather than only swelling or increase.
QIRAAT-ER:41:39:15#1/r1.anchor: H, mutawatir: Canonical ten-reading variant with hamza after bāʾ; it shifts the sound

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p188#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p188#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p188#2/r1.claim: Qatada describes the earth as gray and crumbling.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p188#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ ترى الأرض خاشعة ﴾ قال غبراء متهشمة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r1.claim: The earth is dry and drooping; khashi'a is borrowed from humility in the sense of submission.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r1.anchor: يابسة متعاطفة مستعار من الخشوع بمعنى التذلل

ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r3.claim: The earth moves with growth and swells: before a plant appears, the ground rises and expands, then splits to let the plant emerge.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r3.anchor: أي تحركت بالنبات وانتفخت لأن النبت إذا دنا أن يظهر ارتفعت له الأرض وانتفخت ثم تصدعت عن النبات

ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r4.claim: Al-Alusi prefers a representative simile: the barren earth revived by rain resembles a gloomy, shabby person, ignored until worldly adornment makes him walk proudly; the comparison is omitted while its humbling and swaying features evoke it.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون في الكلام استعارة تمثيلية شبه حال جدوبة الأرض وخلوها عن النبات ثم إحياء الله تعالى إياها بالمطر

ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r5.claim: A variant reads raba'at with hamza, meaning increased; al-Zajjaj says raba means grew greatly, while the hamzated form means rose, as in rabī'a, a lookout on a high place.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r6.claim: The One who revived the earth will revive the dead through resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r6.anchor: بما ذكر بعد موتها ( لمحي الموتى

ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r7.claim: The phrase every thing includes resurrection among the objects of divine power and intensifies the affirmation of that power.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p126#2/r7.anchor: من الأشياء التي من جملتها الإحياء

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:38-40/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:38-40/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:38-40/r3.claim: The earth is dry and low-lying; “humble” is borrowed from submission.
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:38-40/r3.anchor: يابسة متطامنة مستعار من الخشوع بمعنى التذلل

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:38-40/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:38-40/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:38-40/r4.claim: After rain, the earth is adorned with growth and swells.

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:38-40/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:38-40/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:38-40/r5.claim: A variant reads ربأت, meaning rose or increased.

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:38-40/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:38-40/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:38-40/r6.claim: The One reviving the dead earth will revive the dead and can do everything, including give life and death.
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:38-40/r6.anchor: بعد موتها. { لمحى الموتى إنه على كل شىء قدير } من الإحياء والإماتة.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r1.claim: After signs in heaven, some of which are worshiped, the passage turns to earthly signs; unlike Yasin, the context here emphasizes oneness, while Yasin stresses resurrection and the earth’s proof is clearer there.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r1.anchor: ولما ذكر بعض آيات السماء لشرفها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r2.claim: One sees part of the earth directly and apprehends the rest by reasoning from what is visible, since all of it is equally within divine power.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r2.anchor: أي بعضها بحاسة البصر وبعضها بعين البصيرة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r3.claim: The earth is “humble” when dry and bare of vegetation, like a powerless, flattened person.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r3.anchor: أي يابسة لا نبات فيها فهي بصورة الذليل الذي لا منعة عنده

BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r4.claim: Biqāʿī says this depiction is closer to the worshipper’s state than the description previously used in al-Hajj.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r4.anchor: عبر بما هو أقرب إلى حال العابد ما مضى في الحج

BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r5.claim: God’s sending of rain is exclusively His act and one of the strongest signs of the One; the switch to the majestic plural signals power and greatness.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r5.anchor: إنزال الماء مما استأثر به سبحانه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r6.claim: Rain may come from clouds or be driven from high places, bringing soil suitable for growth even to saline land such as Egypt.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r6.anchor: من الغمام أو سقناه إليها من الأماكن العالية

BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r7.claim: The earth “shakes” by moving greatly, abundantly, and quickly, as though it were doing this of its own accord.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r8.claim: The earth cracks and rises; plants emerge, cover its face, branch roots, and thicken stems until passage across it is impeded.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r8.anchor: تشققت فارتفع ترابها وخرج منها النبات

BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r9.claim: As an inward allusion, knowledge waters the soul-earth: remorse bears blessings, shortcomings are pardoned, and obedience, nearness, and divine manifestations adorn and purify it.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r9.anchor: فطرها بمياه المعارف فظهرت فيها بركات الندم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r10.claim: The visible revival of earth proves power to bring the nonexistent into being and restore what decayed and crumbled; reviving the dead is no different.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r10.anchor: دليلا مشاهدا على القدرة على إيجاد المعدوم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r11.claim: God revives the dead just as He brings forth plants after they decayed and became soil.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r11.anchor: الذي كان بلي وتحطم وصار ترابا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r12.claim: Although people acknowledge God’s complete power, their denial of resurrection treats Him as unable; all possible things are equally within complete power.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p577/r12.anchor: الممكنات متساوية الأقدام بالنسبة إلى القدرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r1.claim: This passage continues the creation narrative: created worlds establish God’s exclusive divinity, and the argument now shifts from created entities to their states, moving from celestial conditions to earthly ones.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r2.claim: The discourse returns from third-person narration to direct address, resuming the audience-facing mode used earlier when challenging them about creation.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r3.claim: “Signs” means proofs; they are attributed to God because they demonstrate His existence and oneness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r3.anchor: وإضافتها إلى ضمير الله لأنها دليل على وحدانيته وعلى وجوده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r4.claim: The variation of night and day is a sign of power that no one but God can produce, and so proves His exclusive creative act and divinity; Ibn ʿĀshūr points to the earlier discussion in al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r4.anchor: واختلاف الليل والنهار آية من آيات القدرة التي لا يفعلها غير الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r5.claim: The sun and moon signify their regular, continuing motion here, not their creation, which was already covered by the making of the heavens; the sun is one of the seven heavens and the moon follows it.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r6.claim: No particular sunrise, setting, or orbit is specified so their conditions of motion remain available as the primary evidence; mentioning their creation also reinforces the earlier statement about the heavens and completes the meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p298/r6.anchor: ولخلقهما تأكيد لما استفيد من قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r1.claim: “Humbled” and “shook” form a personifying metaphor: the earth is pictured as a person first abject, then shaking the shoulders, with each image-part mapped to the earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r1.anchor: مكنية بأن شبهت بشخص كان ذليلا ثم صار مهتزا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r2.claim: “It shook” points to vegetation appearing and moving on the earth; “it swelled” adds that the earth puffs up with water and rises.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r2.anchor: لأن المقصود من الاهتزاز هو ظهور النبات عليها وتحركه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r3.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads the word with a hamza after the bāʾ, from the hamzated verb meaning “to rise.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r3.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر { وربأت } بهمزة بعد الموحدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r4.claim: The resurrection proof is embedded within the argument for God’s exclusive creation and governance, following the Qur’an’s varied style and use of opportunities to guide toward truth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r4.anchor: إدماج لإثبات البعث في أثناء الاستدلال على تفرده تعالى بالخلق والتدبير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r5.claim: The resurrection statement begins a new sentence; the analogy between two acts of revivification motivates it, and emphasis answers the audience’s denial of raising the dead.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r5.anchor: والجملة استئناف ابتدائي والمناسبة مشابهة الإحياءين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r6.claim: The relative form of the subject explains the predicate: rain brings seeds inside the earth to sprout, and this is metaphorically called “reviving” the earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r6.anchor: وتعريف المسند إليه بالموصولية لما في الموصول من تعليل الخبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r7.claim: Reviving earth by rain supplies a likeness-based argument for the possibility of resurrecting the dead; this analogy draws the conclusion closer but is persuasive rather than demonstrative, fitting the deniers’ appeal to customary improbability.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r7.anchor: ثم ارتقي من ذلك إلى جعل ذلك الذي سمي إحياء لأنه شبيه الإحياء دليلا على إمكان إحياء الموتى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r8.claim: The closing affirmation that God has power over everything makes this otherwise persuasive analogy forceful: the creator alone can perform both the lesser and greater act, so neither exceeds His power.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p302/r8.anchor: فالمشبه به حيث كان لا يقدر على فعله إلا الخالق الذي اتصف بالقدرة التامة لذاته

BURSEVI:v8p204/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p204/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p204/r1.claim: The earth's reviving is one of the proofs of God's power.

BURSEVI:v8p204/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p204/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p204/r2.claim: The address in you see can be to Muhammad or to any observer.
BURSEVI:v8p204/r2.anchor: {أنك} يا محمد أو يا أيها الناظر.

BURSEVI:v8p204/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p204/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p204/r3.claim: The earth is dry, bare of plants, and low or flattened.
BURSEVI:v8p204/r3.anchor: {ترى الارض} : حال كونها {خاشعة} يابسة لا نبات فيها متطامنة

BURSEVI:v8p204/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p204/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p204/r4.claim: The word borrows humility imagery: barren, fruitless land is likened to a humble, lowly person ignored for their diminished appearance.
BURSEVI:v8p204/r4.anchor: مستعار من الخشوع بمعنى التذلل شبه يبس الأرض وخلوها عن الخير والبركة بكون الشخص خاشعا ذليلا

BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r1.claim: Ihtazzat means it moved, here by producing vegetation.
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r1.anchor: {فإذآ أنزلنا عليها المآء اهتزت} : الاهتزاز : التحرك ؛ أي : تحركت بالنبات

BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r2.claim: The ground swells as a plant nears emergence, then rises and splits; rabā means to increase and grow, and a horse may swell after running or fright.
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r2.anchor: {وربت} : وانتفخت ؛ لأن النبت إذا دنا أن يظهر ارتفعت له الأرض ، وانتفخت ثم تصدعت عن النبات

BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r3.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r3.claim: Al-Rāghib glosses rabat as increasing like a thing nurtured to grow.
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r3.anchor: وقال الراغب : وربت ؛ أي : زادت زيادة المتربي.

BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r4.claim: The earth's life-giving is really the stirring of its growth powers and renewal of its freshness through varied plants.
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r4.anchor: {إن الذى أحياها} بما ذكر بعد موتها والإحياء في الحقيقة إعطاء الحياة ، وهي صفة تقتضي الحس والحركة ، فالمراد بإحياء الأرض تهييج القوى النامية فيها

BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r5.claim: The revival of dead earth points to resurrection: God can revive the dead, since His power encompasses every thing, including revival.
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r5.anchor: {فانظر إلى} بالبعث. {أنه على كل شىء} من الأشياء التي من جملتها الإحياء.

BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r6.claim: Qadīr intensifies the statement of God's power; He has promised resurrection and will fulfill it, with recompense as the wisdom behind reviving the dead.
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r6.anchor: {قدير} مبالغ في القدرة وقد وعد بذلك من أن يفي به والحكمة في الإحياء هو المجازاة والمكافأة.

BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r7.claim: The earth of human nature dries when motives and means are absent; rain of trial and istidrāj makes it stir with sins and forbidden acts.
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r7.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى إحياء النفوس وإحياء القلوب. أما الأول فلأن أرض البشرية قد تصير يابسة عند فقدان الدواعي والأسباب

BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r8.claim: A Mathnawī fragment likens the dormant ego to a dragon, apparently subdued by deprivation but not truly dead.
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r8.anchor: آتشت هيزم فرعون نيست زانكه جون فرعون اوراعون نيست نفس ازدرهاست اوكى مرده است

BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r9.claim: The hardest prayer directed at the self is to taste itself: self-delight distracts from the goal and leaves no hope of success.
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r9.anchor: ولذا كان أصعب دعاء إليه أن يقال له : أذاقك الله طعم نفسك

BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r10.claim: Hearts revive through faith's light, sincere seeking, and strong longing when grace's rain and mercy water them.
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r10.anchor: الطلب وغلبات الشوق ، وذلك عند نزول مطر اللطف وماء الرحمة.

BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r11.speaker: بعض الصالحين
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r11.claim: A righteous observer says he saw Samnūn swaying during the circumambulation; at a question about standing before God, Samnūn fainted and, on waking, recited a poem.
BURSEVI:v8p204#2/r11.anchor: وعن بعض الصالحين قال : رأيت سمنون في الطواف ، وهو يتمايل ، فقبضت على يده.

MUQATIL:41:39-40/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:41:39-40/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:41:39-40/r1.claim: God’s created works make His oneness known, even though people do not see Him.
MUQATIL:41:39-40/r1.anchor: أن يعرف التوحيد بصنعه، وإن لم تروه

MUQATIL:41:39-40/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:41:39-40/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:41:39-40/r2.claim: The earth is dry, dusty, broken up, and without vegetation.

MUQATIL:41:39-40/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:41:39-40/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:41:39-40/r3.claim: Rain makes the dead earth live and sprout; it shakes with greenery and increases its plants.

MUQATIL:41:39-40/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:41:39-40/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:41:39-40/r4.claim: The One who revived earth after death will revive the dead in the Hereafter, teaching anyone who doubts resurrection.
MUQATIL:41:39-40/r4.anchor: إن الذي أحياها } بعد موتها، { لمحي الموتى } في الآخرة، ليعتبر من يشك في البعث

MUQATIL:41:39-40/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:41:39-40/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:41:39-40/r5.claim: God has power over resurrection and everything else.
MUQATIL:41:39-40/r5.anchor: إنه على كل شيء قدير } [آية: 39] من البعث وغيره

NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#4/r1.claim: The earth is dry and changed; khushūʿ literally denotes submission and is applied metaphorically to barren land with no growth.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#4/r1.anchor: يابسة مغيرة والخسوع التذلل فاستعير لحال الأرض اذا كانت قحطة لانبات فيها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#4/r2.claim: The water is rain; the earth stirs with vegetation and swells.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p91#4/r3.claim: The One who revived the earth will necessarily be able to resurrect the dead, since He has power over everything.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r1.claim: A khāshiʿa land is gray and grows vegetation; a khāshiʿ town or place is dusty and uninhabited.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r1.anchor: والأرض الخاشعة: الغبراء التي تنبت. وبلدة خاشعة: أي مغبرة لا منزل بها.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r2.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r2.claim: Mujāhid says the land “shakes” by producing vegetation; ihtazz also means to move, as a person does.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r2.anchor: أي بالنبات قاله مجاهد. يقال: اهتز الإنسان أي تحرك

QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r3.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r3.claim: A poet compares a person shaking for generosity to a sword blade quivering for dew, illustrating the sense of movement in ihtazz.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r3.anchor: ومنه: تراه كنصل السيف يهتز للندى إذا لم تجد عند امرىء السوء مطمعا

QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r4.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r4.claim: Mujāhid explains rabat as swelling and rising before the vegetation emerges.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r4.anchor: أي انتفخت وعلت قبل أن تنبت قاله مجاهد.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r5.claim: On the explanation that the earth rises above the vegetation after its death, the wording puts events out of order: the sequence is rabat then ihtazzat.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r5.anchor: أي تصعدت عن النبات بعد موتها. وعلى هذا التقدير يكون في الكلام تقديم وتأخير وتقديره: ربت واهتزت.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r6.claim: Shaking and swelling may occur before shoots emerge or after plants reach the surface; growth raises the earth, while vegetation first moves outward and then expands in height, length and width.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r6.anchor: والاهتزاز والربو قد يكونان قبل الخروج من الأرض وقد يكونان بعد خروج النبات إلى وجه الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r7.claim: Rabat can mean rising, as shown by the names rabwa and rābiya for raised ground.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r7.anchor: فربوها ارتفاعها. ويقال للموضع المرتفع: ربوة ورابية

QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر وخالد
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r8.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and Khālid read warabaʾat with hamza, meaning that the earth grew or increased, from al-rabīʾa.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وخالد «وربأت» ومعناه عظمت من الربيئة.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r9.claim: Another explanation says the earth rejoices at rain when it shakes and swells with vegetation; since splitting for plants is described as laughing, the earth may likewise be described as rejoicing.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r9.anchor: وقيل: «اهتزت» أي استبشرت بالمطر «وربت» أي انتفخت بالنبات. والأرض إذا انشقت بالنبات: وصفت بالضحك،

QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r10.claim: A further view treats swelling and shaking as one state: the emergence of vegetation.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r10.anchor: ويجوز أن يقال الربو والاهتزاز واحد وهي حالة خروج النبات.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r11.claim: Al-Qurṭubī links this revival-of-earth argument to the treatment of the same meaning in Sūrat al-Ḥajj.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r12.claim: The God who revives dead earth will revive the dead, for He has power over everything.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:39/r12.anchor: { إن الذي أحياها لمحى الموتى إنه على كل شيء قدير }

RAZI-FULL:v27p112#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p112#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p112#2/r1.claim: “Humble” means subdued and diminished; the word is metaphorically applied to earth when it lacks rain and vegetation.
RAZI-FULL:v27p112#2/r1.anchor: والخشوع التذلل والتصاغر ، واستعير هذا اللفظ

RAZI-FULL:v27p112#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p112#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p112#2/r2.claim: The earth stirs with new growth and swells as plants approach emergence, lifting and splitting the soil.
RAZI-FULL:v27p112#2/r2.anchor: أي تحركت بالنبات ، وربت : انتفخت لأن النبت

RAZI-FULL:v27p112#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p112#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p112#2/r3.claim: The One who revives dead earth can revive dead bodies; the earth’s renewal is evidence for bodily resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v27p112#2/r3.anchor: يعني أن القادر على إحياء الأرض بعد موتها هو القادر على إحياء هذه الأجساد بعد موتها

RAZI-FULL:v27p112#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p112#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p112#2/r4.claim: Reassembling scattered bodily parts is possible, as is restoring life, intellect, and ability to them; since God can do all possibilities, bodily resurrection is plainly possible.
RAZI-FULL:v27p112#2/r4.anchor: عودة التأليف والتركيب إلى تلك الأجزاء المتفرقة ممكن لذاته

STUDYQURAN:41:39/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:39/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:41:39/r1.claim: God's reviving barren land is an argument for His ability to resurrect human beings, as in many other verses.
STUDYQURAN:41:39/r1.anchor: This is one of several verses to invoke God’s ability to revive barren land as an argument for His ability to resurrect human beings

STUDYQURAN:41:39/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:39/r2.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:41:39/r2.claim: The revived land can symbolize a soul dried by heedlessness and ignorance, stirred by the water of life or wine of Divine Love and revived through God's remembrance and knowledge.
STUDYQURAN:41:39/r2.anchor: is revived by the remembrance of God and knowledge of Him (Aj).

STUDYQURAN:41:39/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:39/r3.speaker: al-Qushayrī
STUDYQURAN:41:39/r3.claim: Al-Qushayrī reads the verse as a heart drawing near to God when humbled by awareness of sin and then displaying the blessings of regret and repentance.
STUDYQURAN:41:39/r3.anchor: al-Qushayrī sees this verse as a metaphor for the condition of a heart to which God draws near

TAB-FULL:v20p438/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r1.claim: The revival of barren land is evidence that God can raise the dead and restore them after they have decayed.
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r1.anchor: ومن حجج الله أيضا وأدلته على قدرته على نشر الموتى من بعد بلاها، وإعادتها لهيئتها كما كانت من بعد فنائها

TAB-FULL:v20p438/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r2.claim: Qatada glosses the humbled earth as gray and broken.
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ومن آياته أنك ترى الأرض خاشعة} [فصلت: 39] «أي غبراء متهشمة»

TAB-FULL:v20p438/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r3.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the humbled earth as dry and crumbling.
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r3.anchor: عن السدي، {ومن آياته أنك ترى الأرض خاشعة} [فصلت: 39] قال: «يابسة متهمشة»

TAB-FULL:v20p438/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r4.claim: When rain from the sky falls on the barren land, it stirs as vegetation grows; the same wording appears in 22:5.
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r4.anchor: فإذا أنزلنا من السماء غيثا على هذه الأرض الخاشعة اهتزت بالنبات. يقول: تحركت به

TAB-FULL:v20p438/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r5.claim: Mujahid explains that the earth stirs with vegetation.

TAB-FULL:v20p438/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r8.claim: Qatada says rain is recognized in the land's surface and swelling.
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r8.anchor: عن قتادة، {فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت وربت} [الحج: 5] «يعرف الغيث في سحتها وربوها»

TAB-FULL:v20p438/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r9.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r9.claim: Mujahid associates the swelling with plants and says the earth rises before they sprout.
TAB-FULL:v20p438/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد، {وربت} [فصلت: 39] " للنبات، قال: «ارتفعت قبل أن تنبت»

TAB-FULL:v20p439/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p439/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p439/r1.claim: The God who revives barren land and brings out plants by rain can revive dead human beings after their death.
TAB-FULL:v20p439/r1.anchor: عن السدي، قال: «كما يحيي الأرض بالمطر، كذلك يحيي الموتى بالماء يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v20p439/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p439/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p439/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says that just as rain revives earth, water revives the dead between the two trumpet blasts on Resurrection Day.
TAB-FULL:v20p439/r2.anchor: عن السدي، قال: «كما يحيي الأرض بالمطر، كذلك يحيي الموتى بالماء يوم القيامة بين النفختين»

TAB-FULL:v20p439/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p439/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p439/r3.claim: God can revive creation after death and do anything He wills; nothing He intends defeats or eludes His power.
TAB-FULL:v20p439/r3.anchor: إن ربك يا محمد على إحياء خلقه بعد مماتهم وعلى كل ما يشاء ذو قدرة لا يعجزه شيء أراده، ولا يتعذر عليه فعل شيء شاءه

SULAMI:v2p220#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p220#2/r1.speaker: عمرو بن عثمان المكي
SULAMI:v2p220#2/r1.claim: Amr ibn Uthman likens hearts to earth: God's mercy, gaze, and beneficence awaken hidden deposits, producing humility before God, awe among people, compassion, counsel, and lasting fear of sin; the One who revives these souls can revive inattentive hearts and those dead to service.
SULAMI:v2p220#2/r1.anchor: قال عمرو بن عثمان المكي : إن لله عز وجل قلوبا في الأوعية من الأجسام أودع بها ودائع وأخفاها على الخلق

TABATABAI:41:38-39/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:38-39/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:38-39/r4.claim: Khushūʿ is humility, ihtizāz is intense movement, and rubū is growth, flourishing, and rising.

TABATABAI:41:38-39/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:38-39/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:38-39/r5.claim: The earth’s shaking and rising describe its plants moving and growing upward.
TABATABAI:41:38-39/r5.anchor: واهتزاز الأرض وربوها تحركها بنباتها وارتفاعه

TABATABAI:41:38-39/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:38-39/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:38-39/r6.claim: A representative metaphor compares barren earth turning green to a poor, shabby person transformed by wealth into a splendid, lively figure.
TABATABAI:41:38-39/r6.anchor: وفي الآية استعارة تمثيلية شبهت فيها الأرض في جدبها وخلوها عن النبات ثم اخضرارها ونمو نباتها وعلوه بشخص

TABATABAI:41:38-39/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:38-39/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:38-39/r7.claim: The earth’s revival argues for resurrection; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this argument was discussed in earlier sūras.

TABRISI:41:39-42/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:39-42/r1.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:41:39-42/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi explains that the earth stirs with vegetation and grows through abundant crop yield.
TABRISI:41:39-42/r1.anchor: اهتزت بالنبات { وربت } بكثرة ريعها عن الكلبي

TABRISI:41:39-42/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:39-42/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:39-42/r2.claim: God revived the earth with rain and will likewise revive the dead at the resurrection.
TABRISI:41:39-42/r2.anchor: لمحي الموتى } في الآخرة مثل ذلك

TABRISI:41:39-42/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:39-42/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:39-42/r3.anchor: إنه على كل شيء قدير } ظاهر المعنى

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:41:39-43/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:41:39-43/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:41:39-43/r1.claim: The earth is barren and dusty, with no plants.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:41:39-43/r1.anchor: مغبرة لا نبات فيها { فإذا أنزلنا عليهم الماء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:41:39-43/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:41:39-43/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:41:39-43/r2.claim: The earth moves with vegetation, swells and rises, then splits open to produce plants.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:41:39-43/r2.anchor: تحركت بالنبات { وربت } انتفخت وعلت، ثم تصدعت عن النبات

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:39/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:39/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:39/r1.claim: Arab polytheists’ denial of the afterlife, accountability, and resurrection is answered by recalling that the power which revives barren earth can also raise the dead.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:39/r1.anchor: Müşrik Araplar’ın İslâm karşısındaki temel bir tutumları da herkesin bu dünyada benimsediği inanç ve davranışlarının hesabını vereceği âhiret hayatını, dolayısıyla yeniden dirilmeyi inkâr etmeleriydi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:39/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:39/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:39/r2.claim: God’s power to revive the dead is stated absolutely, affirming his power to resurrect people after death.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:39/r2.anchor: Âyette kuru toprağa can veren gücün insanı yeniden diriltmeye de muktedir olduğu hatırlatılmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:39/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:39/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:39/r3.claim: Because the life-giving power is expressed absolutely, the verse may also mean that God gives every positive capacity and activity: vitality, health, productivity, mental clarity, and an enlightened heart.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:39/r3.anchor: burada sadece insanların öldükten sonra diriltilmesi kastedilmeyip bunun yanında mutlak olarak canlılık, sağlık, zindelik, verimlilik, üretkenlik, zihin açıklığı, kalp aydınlığı gibi her türlü olumlu yetenek ve aktiviteleri verenin Allah olduğuna işaret edildiği de düşünülebilir.

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p320/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p320/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p320/r3.claim: Calling the earth alive refers figuratively to its greenness, freshness, and flowering, while saying that God revives it is a literal attribution.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p320/r3.anchor: جعل خضرة الأرض ونضرتها وبهجتها بما يظهره الله تعالى فيها من النبات والأنوار والأزهار وعجائب الصنع حياة لها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p64/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p64/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p64/r1.claim: Wealth is sought for beneficial use, not possession alone; a rich miser who never benefits from it is poor in the relevant sense.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p64/r1.anchor: وأما قولهم في الغنى إذا كان بخيلا لا ينتفع بماله إن غناء فقر فهو في الضرب الأول أعنى تنزيل الوجود منزلة العدم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p64/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p64/r2.speaker: اللؤماء
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p64/r2.claim: The claim that a miser still benefits from imagined future access or a sense of security is rejected as wishful self-excuse; wealth can instead bring humiliation and torment.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p64/r2.anchor: وأما قول اللؤماء إن انتفاعه في اعتقاده أنه متى شاء انتفع به وما يجد في نفسه من عزة الاستظهار

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p64/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p64/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p64/r3.claim: The author compares this excuse to an oppressor boasting of power: the one who validates such a boast is more blameworthy than the one who denies it and hopes for the oppressor's reform.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p64/r3.anchor: وترى المصدق له في دعواه أذم له وأهجى من المكذب لأن الذى صدقه أيس من أن ينزع إلى الإنسانية بحال

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p64/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p64/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p64/r4.claim: Contentment is genuine wealth and greed makes its possessor poor; this is substantively true even when phrased as a comparison.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p64/r4.anchor: إن القناعة فاعلمن غنى والحرص يورث أهله الفقرا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r1.claim: A simile gains finesse when it finds a likeness across different kinds of things, carrying an image from a distant domain into a new one.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r1.anchor: أن لتصور الشبه من الشيء في غير جنسه وشكله والتقاط ذلك له من غير محلته واجتلابه إليه من النيق البعيد بابا آخر من الظرف واللطف

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r2.claim: Even the familiar eye-and-narcissus comparison spans different kinds; comparisons of the Pleiades to a flowering grape cluster, silver bridle, or necklace are more particular examples.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r2.anchor: العين بالنرجس عامي مشترك معروف في أجيال الناس جار في جميع العادات

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r3.claim: The more distant the compared things, the more astonishing and pleasing the simile, and the more likely it is to awaken delight.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r3.anchor: وهكذا إذا استقريت التشبيهات وجدت التباعد بين الشيئين كلما كان أشد كانت إلى النفوس أعجب وكانت النفوس لها أطرب

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r4.claim: The cited poem makes the blue violet resemble early flames on sulfur tips among red gems; this distant likeness is stranger and more captivating than comparing narcissus to jeweled bowls.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r4.anchor: تزهو بزرقتها بين الرياض على حمر اليواقيت

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r5.claim: An object appearing in an unfamiliar place or form fascinates more; comparing violet to another plant or colored object would lose this strangeness and beauty.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p108/r5.anchor: ولو أنه شبه البنفسج ببعض النبات أو صادف له شبها في شىء من المتلونات لم تجد له هذه الغرابة ولم ينل من الحسن هذا الحظ

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286#2/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286#2/r1.claim: Reading the poem as a simple comparison with the known moon absurdly makes that moon light the earth while leaving the speaker's saddle dark.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286#2/r1.anchor: وبدر اضاء الأرض شرقا ومغربا وموضع رحلي منه اسود مظلم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286#2/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286#2/r2.claim: Al-Buḥturī treats the praised man as an already established moon and invents a new moon-like being with the astonishing trait of leaving one spot dark.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286#2/r2.anchor: فالبحتري في قوله وبدر اضاء الأرض قد بنى كلامه على أن كون الممدوح بدرا أمر قد استقر وثبت

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286#2/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286#2/r3.claim: This rhetorical construction resists كاف, كأن, تحسب, and تخال because those forms introduce an uncertain relation to an otherwise understood predicate.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286#2/r3.anchor: وكما يمتنع دخول الكاف في هذا النحو كذلك يمتنع دخول كأن وتحسب وتخال

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286#2/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286#2/r4.claim: These verbs suit a predicate already known in general but uncertainly attached to the subject, or a familiar metaphor; here the described phenomenon itself is unknown.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286#2/r4.anchor: وجه بعده من القبول بين وهو أن كان وحسبت وخلت وظننت تدخل إذا كان الخبر والمفعول الثاني امرا معقولا ثابتا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p91/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p91/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p91/r1.claim: The image of the neighborhood's ravines flowing toward him gains its beauty from the original placement of the adverbials; rearranging them removes its sweetness and emotional effect.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p91/r1.anchor: سالت عليه شعاب الحي حين دعا أنصاره بوجوه كالدنانير

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p91/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p91/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p91/r2.claim: A passage may gain merit from wording, from composition, or from both; when both contribute, readers often wrongly credit the wording alone, and metaphorical merit may require understanding نظم.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p91/r2.anchor: كلاما حسنه للفظ دون النظم ، وآخر حسنه للنظم دون اللفظ

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p91/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p91/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p91/r3.claim: The force of واشْتَعَلَ الرَّأْسُ شَيْبًا is not metaphor alone: the verb is predicated of something related to the true agent, شيبا, which follows in the accusative to clarify that relation.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p91/r3.anchor: ولكن لأن سلك بالكلام طريق ما يسند الفعل فيه إلى الشيء ، وهو لما هو من سببه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p190/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p190/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p190/r1.claim: A coordinated set of clauses functioning as a condition must be parsed jointly; its parts form one grammatical whole, just as both parts of a predicate, adjective, or circumstantial phrase do.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p190/r1.anchor: فكما يكون الخبر والصفة والحال لا محالة في مجموع الجزءين لا في أحدهما كذلك يكون الشرط في مجموع الجملتين

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p242/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p242/r1.speaker: ابن الأنباري
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p242/r1.claim: Ibn al-Anbari reports that al-Kindi called three forms redundant; Abu al-Abbas answered that they respectively assert, answer a question, and answer a denial, so their meanings differ.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p242/r1.anchor: روي عن ابن الأنباري أنه قال : ركب الكندي المتفلسف

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p242/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p242/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p242/r2.claim: The particle إن binds the following clause to what precedes so the two cohere as one utterance; removing it makes them separate, and فاء does not restore the same relation.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p242/r2.anchor: الجملة إذا هي دخلت ترتبط بما قبلها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p242/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p242/r3.speaker: بشار
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p242/r3.claim: Bashshar’s line about starting early uses إن to show how the second clause becomes closely integrated with the first.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p242/r3.anchor: في بيت بشار : ( بكرا صاحبي قبل الهجير إن ذاك النجاح في التبكير )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p242/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p242/r4.speaker: بعض العرب
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p242/r4.claim: An anonymous Arab’s line about camel-song supplies a second poetic example of إن joining the clauses into a cohesive statement.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p242/r4.anchor: من قول بعض العرب : ( فغنها وهي لك الفداء إن غناء الإبل الحداء )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p275/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p275/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p275/r1.claim: Rhetorical merit belongs to the form in which meaning is expressed, not to bare words as sounds; descriptions such as elegance or ornament name qualities of that form and its effect on meaning.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p275/r1.anchor: نسبوا ما كان من الحسن والمزية في صورة المعنى إلى اللفظ

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p387/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p387/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p387/r1.claim: Adding an object changes a transitive verb’s meaning rather than appending a separate fact; the object shapes what action is asserted, as an adjective shapes a noun’s reference.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p387/r1.anchor: أنهم قد أصلوا في المفعول وكل ما زاد على جزءي الجملة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p387/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p387/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p387/r3.claim: The proverb about a person’s speech and courage, and the example إن أتاك زيد أتاك لحاجة, illustrate how the second verb can acquire a distinct sense through its added qualification or object.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p387/r3.anchor: المرء بأصغريه إن قال قال ببيان وإن صال صال بجنان

TABRISI:41:36-39/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:36-39/r20.speaker: قتادة والسدي
TABRISI:41:36-39/r20.claim: Qatāda and al-Suddī explain the humbled earth as dusty, worn out, and broken down.
TABRISI:41:36-39/r20.anchor: أي غبراء دارسة متهشمة عن قتادة والسدي

TABRISI:41:36-39/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:36-39/r21.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:41:36-39/r21.claim: Another explanation calls it dead and dry with no vegetation; al-Azharī says dry earth without rain is described as humbled.
TABRISI:41:36-39/r21.anchor: وقيل: ميتة يابسة لا نبات فيها قال الأزهري إذا يبست الأرض ولم تمطر

TABRISI:41:36-39/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:36-39/r22.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:36-39/r22.claim: When water falls, the earth stirs with vegetation, swells, and rises before the plants sprout.
TABRISI:41:36-39/r22.anchor: أي تحركت بالنبات وربت أي انتفخت وارتفعت قبل أن تنبت

QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r7.claim: As rain revives parched winter earth, awareness of sin humbles hearts; God turns toward them, bringing the blessings of regret and forgiving their failures in sincerity.
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r7.anchor: وكذلك القلوب إذا خشعت لاستشعارها بما ألمت به من الذنوب أقبل عليها الحق سبحانه ، فظهر فيها بركات الندم

QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r8.claim: When a servant lapses in spiritual practice or leaves the ground of obedience, God’s reminder brings lights of concord, restores the accustomed station, and makes the branch of fidelity fresh again.
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r8.anchor: ثم تغمده الحق - سبحانه - بما يدخل عليه من التذكر تظهر في القلب أنوار الوفاق ، فيعود إلى مألوف مقامه

QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r9.claim: If gnostics pause or suffer a veil because of bad etiquette, God’s caring regard makes their gardens of intimacy stir, their scenes of nearness green, and their impediments retreat.
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r9.anchor: وكذلك إذا بدت لأهل العرفان وقفة ، أو حدثت لهم من جراء سوء أدب بدر منهم حجبة ثم نظر الحق - سبحانه - إليهم بالرعاية

QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r10.claim: The One who revives dead earth can raise the dead, and He can also revive hearts with the light of care after spiritual slackness and veiling.
QUSHAYRI:v3p152/r10.anchor: إن الذي أحيا الأرض بعد موتها قادر على إحياء النفوس بالحشر والنشر

NAHHAS:v4p62/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p62/r9.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v4p62/r9.claim: Sībawayh parses أن as a nominative subject; the preceding material licenses it despite his general rule against starting with أن.
NAHHAS:v4p62/r9.anchor: أن في موضع رفع بالابتداء عند سيبويه وإن كان لا يجيز أن يكون أن في أول الكلام

NAHHAS:v4p62/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p62/r10.speaker: المازني
NAHHAS:v4p62/r10.claim: Al-Māzinī supplies an implicit verb to govern what cannot begin independently, estimating كيف استقر زيد.
NAHHAS:v4p62/r10.anchor: والرفع عند المازني بإضمار فعل فيما لا يجوز أن يبتدأ به كما تقول كيف زيد

NAHHAS:v4p62/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p62/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p62/r11.claim: خاشعة is parsed as a circumstantial accusative.
NAHHAS:v4p62/r11.anchor: خاشعة منصوبة على الحال ( فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت وربت )

NAHHAS:v4p62/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p62/r12.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v4p62/r12.claim: Sībawayh derives ربت from ربا يربو and gives its dual as ربوان.
NAHHAS:v4p62/r12.anchor: من ربا يربو فحذفت الألف لسكونها وسكون التاء بعدها ويقال في تثنية ربا ربوان كذا قال سيبويه

NAHHAS:v4p62/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p62/r13.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v4p62/r13.claim: The Kufans give the dual as ربيان and write ربا with yāʾ.
NAHHAS:v4p62/r13.anchor: والكوفيون يقولون ربيان بالياء ويكتبون ربا بالياء

NAHHAS:v4p62/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p62/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p62/r14.claim: Abū Jaʿfar favors the Basran analysis, saying the Qurʾanic form supports it; Abū Isḥāq rebukes the Kufans for extending a spelling error to the dual.
NAHHAS:v4p62/r14.anchor: قال أبو جعفر وسمعت أبا إسحاق يقول ليس يكفيهم أن يغلطوا في الخط حتى يتجاوزوا ذلك إلى التثنية

NAHHAS:v4p62/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p62/r15.speaker: أبو جعفر
NAHHAS:v4p62/r15.claim: A recitation attributed to Abū Jaʿfar has اهتزت وربأت, derived from the word for a lookout who rises to a high place.
NAHHAS:v4p62/r15.anchor: وقراءة أبي جعفر ( اهتزت وربأت ) وهو مأخوذ من الربيئة

NAHHAS:v4p62/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p62/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p62/r16.claim: ربأت means “rose,” from the verb for ascending to a high lookout position.
NAHHAS:v4p62/r16.anchor: إذا ارتفع إلى موضع عال يرقب فمعنى وربأت ارتفعت

NAHHAS:v4p62/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p62/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p62/r17.claim: In لمحيي, the yāʾ loses its ḍamma because it is heavy, then a yāʾ is deleted where two sukūns meet.
NAHHAS:v4p62/r17.anchor: حذفت الضمة من الياء لثقلها ثم حذفت الياء لالتقاء الساكنين

ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r6.claim: The earth is crumbling and changed, like hāmida.
ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r6.anchor: أي متهشمة متغيرة، وهو مثل هامدة

ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r7.claim: The verb is also read with hamza as rabaʾat.
ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r7.anchor: ويقرأ وربأت بالهمز، ومعنى ربت عظمت

ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r8.claim: Rabat means grew or swelled, while rabaʾat means rose as the ground lifts when plants are about to emerge.
ZAJJAJ:v4p387/r8.anchor: ومعنى ربت عظمت، ومعنى ربأت ارتفعت لأن النبت إذا هم أن يظهر ارتفعت له الأرض

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#2/r11.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#2/r11.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#2/r11.claim: In Fussilat's worship setting, 'humbled' suits the earth; the verse stops at its stirring and swelling because sprouting and emergence do not suit the scene of worship.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#2/r11.anchor: إن الجو في السياق الثاني هو جو عبادة وخشوع يتسق معه تصوير الأرض بأنها خاشعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p175#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p175#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p175#2/r5.claim: The earth is khāshiʿa when it is dry, dusty, and without vegetation.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p175#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p175#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p175#2/r6.claim: Water makes the earth stir and swell; the One who revives it is able to raise the dead and is powerful over everything.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p175#2/r6.anchor: فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت وربت إن الذي أحياها لمحيي الموتى إنه على كل شيء قدير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r5.claim: The parched earth’s drooping and roughness under drought and scorching wind make it look downcast, like someone nearly weeping; its revival points from a visible sign to resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r5.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى آية منصوبة ليعتبر بها في أمر البعث من القبور، ويستدل بما شوهد من هذه على ما لم يشاهد بعد من تلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r6.claim: The earth’s khushūʿ is its visible barrenness and roughness during drought and the dryness of scorching winds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r6.anchor: وخشوع الأرض هو ما يظهر عليها من استكانة وشعث بالجدب وصليم السموم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r7.claim: The water sent down is rain.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r8.claim: The earth’s movement is its parts loosening with water and cracking open for plants.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r8.anchor: واهتزاز الأرض: هو تخلخل أجزائها بالماء وتشققها للنبات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r9.claim: Rabwahā means its swelling with water and the rise of its surface.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r9.anchor: وربوها: هو انتفاخها بالماء وعلو سطحها به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r11.speaker: أبو جعفر بن القعقاع والرؤاسي عن أبي عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r11.claim: Abu Jaʿfar ibn al-Qaʿqaʿ reads rabāʾat with hamza; al-Ruʾasi reports the same from Abu ʿAmr. It means rose or became elevated, like al-rabīʾa, a lookout set on high ground.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r12.claim: The revival of dead earth is the sign by which people should infer that God can revive the dead.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r12.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى بالأمر الذي ينبغي أن يقاس على هذه الآية والعبرة، وذلك إحياء الموتى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r13.claim: The statement is general, and in the language a “thing” means an existent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p17/r13.anchor: وقوله تعالى: إنه على كل شيء قدير عموم، والشيء في اللغة: الموجود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p182#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p182#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p182#2/r1.claim: A barren, plantless earth revives and produces varied crops and fruits after rain; its revival demonstrates God’s power to resurrect the dead and His power over all things.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p182#2/r1.anchor: هامدة لا نبات فيها، بل هي ميتة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r6.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r6.claim: Qatada glosses the earth as dusty and worn out.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r7.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r7.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the earth as dead and dry.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r8.claim: The earth is humbled by drought when abandoned, but flourishing and esteemed when inhabited.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r8.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : ذليلة بالجدب لأنها مهجورة , وهي إذا أخصبت عزيزة لأنها معمورة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r9.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r9.claim: Mujahid says the earth moves as plants emerge and rises beforehand; his reading reverses the stated order to “rose, then moved.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r9.anchor: أحدهما : اهتزت بالحركة للنبات , وربت بالارتفاع قبل أن تنبت , قاله مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r10.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r10.claim: Al-Kalbi says the earth stirs with vegetation and rises through abundant yield.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r10.anchor: الثاني : اهتزت بالنبات وربت بكثرة ريعها , قاله الكلبي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r11.claim: The revived earth is observable evidence for deniers that God can raise the dead, reasoning from what is seen to what is unseen.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p183/r11.anchor: جعل ذلك دليلا لمنكري البعث على إحياء الخلق بعد الموت استدلالا بالشاهد على الغائب .

QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:37-39/r19.claim: The address is to every rational person; dry, barren earth is a sign that God brings the dead back to life.

NASHR:v2p325/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p325/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p325/r2.claim: Abu Ja'far reads rabat with an added open hamza after bāʾ in both this verse and Fussilat; the others omit it.
NASHR:v2p325/r2.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر (ربأت) بهمزة مفتوحة بعد الباء في الموضعين
